**Zooming and moving around the terrain graph**

In the Terrain Generator, a mouse wheel or a pinch now zooms the graph around the pointer, from far enough out to see a large graph whole to close enough to read every node's settings; two fingers on a trackpad move it, ⌘+ and ⌘− zoom, ⌘0 goes back to full size, and F, the frame button or a double-click on the empty ground shows the whole graph. The minimap sits at the bottom left, outlines the part in view, moves the view where you click or drag, no longer jumps from side to side, and lets the wheel zoom the graph over it. The viewer's 3D camera keeps its distance as it turns instead of coming closer and going away, its background is plain dark by default (the sky is a choice in its menu), and its resolution can be raised to 2048, 4096 or 8192 samples a side, as the classic graph's preview can, with a word on the memory and time they take. In a node's settings the sliders all start at the same place and stay put as you drag them. While you draw a wire near the Map Output, its folded groups that can take it open by themselves and the inputs that take it glow, so that you find where caves or structures plug in; folded groups say how many inputs they hold. A graph without a Map Output says so, with a button that adds one. Delete removes a selected frame too, and ⌘X cuts nodes in one step you can undo.
